newsitem.title: CHINA: CCT Telecom issues convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: CCT Telecom issues convertible bonds.

text.p: CCT Telecom Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it had agreed to issue HK$100.13 million worth of convertible bonds to private investors.
The bonds, which mature on July 20, 1999, carry the right to convert all or part of the principal amount into new shares at a conversion price of HK$0.672 per share, subject to adjustment.

In the event of full conversion of the principal amount, the company will issue 149 million conversion shares, representing about 9.61 percent of its existing share capital and 8.77 percent of the enlarged share capital.
CCT Telecom said the bonds bear an interest rate of 6.0 percent per annum, payable quarterly.

"This is one of our strategic plans to strengthen our financial position. With the proceeds generated from the issue, we are able to further develop our business through investing and expanding new projects in both Hong Kong and the PRC (People's Republic of China)," managing director Bankee Kwan said in a statement.
He said CCT Telecom was negotiating several communications projects in China and would make an announcement as soon as the investment projects were formally signed.
Trading in CCT Telecom shares was suspended on Monday at the request of the company and was due to resume on Tuesday. The stock rose HK$0.02 to close at HK$0.80 last Friday.
